headline: Pilbara Minerals cratered 7.4% today as the ASX pulled back — but last night's US rally and gold hitting fresh highs give the broader portfolio some breathing room.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: A rough session for PLS, dropping 7.4% to $4.52. Lithium sentiment remains under pressure globally — no specific catalyst in today's news, but the stock continues to reflect weak lithium carbonate prices and investor uncertainty about the EV battery supply chain. This is a long-term speculative hold; the thesis hasn't fundamentally changed today, just ongoing sector pain.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: GOOG had a solid night last session, up 1.5% to $335.45 USD. The broader NASDAQ rallied nearly 1%, lifting tech stocks generally. Alphabet's cloud division reportedly crossed $20B in revenue, keeping investor confidence elevated even amid some concerns about free cash flow. Long-term story remains intact.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft edged up 0.65% to $495.63 USD last night, riding the NASDAQ's positive session. No major specific news — just the general tech tailwind. Microsoft's AI integration across its product suite continues to underpin its premium valuation.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two dipped slightly last night, down 0.69% to $215.47 USD. There's growing buzz around GTA 6 potentially being filmed or set partly in Miami Beach, which is more hype than hard news. The stock remains below your cost basis — it's a long-term play on the GTA 6 release cycle.

movers.name: Global X Artificial Intelligence ETF
movers.note: GXAI slipped a touch today, down 0.37% to $16.25. The ASX had a soft session overall, dragging most ETFs lower. The AI theme remains strong globally (NASDAQ up nearly 1% last night), so today's dip is likely just local market noise.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG slipped 0.45% today in line with the broader ASX pullback. As a diversified fund holding global and Australian equities, it mirrors the market — today's dip reflects the ASX 200's 0.9% fall. Nothing to worry about for a long-term holder.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market Shares ETF
movers.note: VTS nudged up 0.15% today, reflecting last night's positive US session filtering through to the ASX-listed US market ETF. Small move but in the right direction — the S&P 500 was up 0.86% last night.

movers.name: Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE was flat today at $93.02. Emerging markets are caught between Middle East tension (which hurts global trade confidence) and a slightly stronger AUD. No news to move it either way — steady as she goes.

watch_today.title: Pilbara Minerals: Hold through the pain
watch_today.detail: PLS crashed 7.4% today to $4.52 — you're now down about 33% on this position. That stings, but there's no new company-specific disaster driving this; it's ongoing lithium sector weakness. For a long-term holder, selling now would lock in a big loss at the bottom of the cycle. The long-term case for lithium in EVs is still there — sit tight unless you need the capital.

watch_today.title: GXAI: Still underwater, but the AI theme is very much alive
watch_today.detail: GXAI is down 14% from your cost basis, and today's small dip doesn't help. But the AI regulation and development news this weekend — including OpenAI and Anthropic CEOs pushing for government oversight — signals AI is becoming more mainstream and investable, not less. Google's Gemini 3.5 Flash is also putting competitive pressure on rivals. Long-term, this ETF is in the right place. Hold.

watch_today.title: TTWO: GTA 6 hype building — stay patient
watch_today.detail: Take-Two dipped slightly last night but there's fresh buzz around GTA 6 potentially shooting in Miami Beach, adding to the pre-release excitement. The stock is down 7.2% from your cost base, but GTA 6 is still the most anticipated game release in years. This is a long-term play on a mega-franchise — hold and let the release cycle do its work.

watch_today.title: RBA rate decision coming — watch for impact on ASX
watch_today.detail: The Reserve Bank of Australia is meeting this week on the cash rate (Australia's official interest rate, which affects everything from mortgages to bank stocks). The RBA is due to speak ahead of the decision. Markets will be watching closely — any hint of a cut could boost the ASX and your Australian ETF holdings. Keep an eye on Tuesday.

watch_today.title: Oil dropped nearly 2.4% last night — good for inflation, worth watching
watch_today.detail: Crude oil fell to $100.05 USD/barrel after a Saudi pipeline was shut following a drone attack from Iraq — but paradoxically, prices dropped, suggesting markets don't expect a prolonged supply shock. Cheaper oil is generally good for inflation (and therefore good for rate cut hopes). A positive backdrop for your broader portfolio.

watch_today.title: Gold hit $4,409 — a fresh high
watch_today.detail: Gold surged over 1% last night to $4,409 USD/oz, a remarkable level driven by Middle East tensions and uncertainty about US fiscal policy. You don't hold gold directly, but rising gold signals 'risk-off' mood globally. It also supports the case for diversified holdings like VDHG and VGE as safe havens benefit.

world.summary: The Middle East is the dominant global story this weekend — a Saudi oil pipeline was hit by a drone attack from Iraq, Middle East shipping costs are escalating, and Iran is increasingly using military pressure as a bargaining chip. Meanwhile, US domestic politics is muddied over Trump's promised $5,000 'dividend' to Americans, and BRICS nations are urging restraint.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia shuts key oil pipeline after drone attack launched from Iraq
stories.why_it_matters: A drone launched from Iraq struck a major Saudi Arabian oil pipeline over the weekend, forcing Saudi Arabia to shut it down. This is the kind of infrastructure attack that can quickly disrupt global oil supplies — Saudi Arabia is the world's largest oil exporter. While oil prices actually fell last night (suggesting markets think it'll be short-lived), a prolonged shutdown could push fuel prices higher worldwide, including at the bowser here on the Gold Coast.

stories.title: Iran Finds Escalation Is Fruitful Path to Leverage in War With U.S.
stories.why_it_matters: The New York Times reports that Iran has concluded that escalating military and proxy pressure against the US and its allies — rather than negotiating — is actually winning it more leverage in the region. Iran-backed groups have attacked Saudi infrastructure, threatened shipping lanes, and are increasingly emboldened. This is a slow-burn risk for global energy markets and could keep oil prices elevated if tensions worsen.

stories.title: Middle East shipping escalation about to hit every Australian wallet
stories.why_it_matters: SBS warns that the escalating conflict in Middle East shipping lanes — with attacks on cargo vessels — is starting to flow through to Australian consumers. When shipping companies face higher risks, they charge more to transport goods, and those costs end up on supermarket shelves and in retail prices. Think higher prices on imported goods, electronics, and clothing. This is a real-world inflation risk for everyday Aussies.

stories.title: BRICS nations urge 'restraint' in Middle East, smooth flow of global trade
stories.why_it_matters: The BRICS bloc — which includes Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa — issued a joint statement calling for 'restraint' in the Middle East and demanding unimpeded global trade flows. This matters because BRICS now represents a huge chunk of global trade. Their public pressure signals that even countries not aligned with the West are worried about the economic consequences of the conflict spreading.

stories.title: Taxes wouldn't fund $5,000 Trump 'dividend' if Republicans win midterms, says commerce secretary
stories.why_it_matters: Trump has promised every American a $5,000 'dividend' payment if Republicans win the midterm elections — but his own Commerce Secretary has admitted there's no tax plan in place to actually pay for it. This signals potential for large US government borrowing to fund the promise if it goes ahead, which could push US interest rates higher. Higher US rates tend to strengthen the US dollar against the Aussie, which affects the value of your USD-denominated holdings.

markets.summary: The ASX 200 had a rough Sunday session, falling 0.89% to 8,741 — dragged lower by resources and broader caution. But last night in the US, it was a different story: both the S&P 500 and NASDAQ rallied solidly, up 0.86% and 0.96% respectively. Gold surged to $4,409/oz, oil slipped nearly 2.4% to $100, and the Aussie dollar nudged higher to 71.7 US cents.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Fell today on resource sector weakness and global caution around Middle East tensions.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Solid gain last night — tech and growth stocks led the charge.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: Nearly 1% gain last night as AI optimism and solid tech earnings kept buyers engaged.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Fell last night despite the Saudi pipeline attack — markets betting on a short disruption.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Gold surged last night to a remarkable level, driven by Middle East tension and US fiscal uncertainty.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: The Aussie edged higher — traders slightly more optimistic about the domestic outlook ahead of the RBA meeting.

politics.summary: Australian domestic politics this week centres on the RBA's upcoming interest rate decision, internal Labor tension over economic management, and a surprise backflip on plastic packaging laws that's drawn rare, widespread criticism.

stories.title: RBA to speak ahead of crucial cash rate meeting
stories.why_it_matters: The Reserve Bank of Australia is set to speak publicly before its next cash rate meeting — the official interest rate decision that affects home loans, savings accounts, and business borrowing across the country. Markets will be listening closely for any hints about whether a rate cut (or hold) is coming. A cut would be good news for mortgage holders and could give the ASX a boost. This is the most market-moving domestic event of the week.

stories.title: 'Don't insult me': Labor luminary unleashes over falling house prices, real wages
stories.why_it_matters: A senior Labor figure has gone public with frustration about the government's economic record — specifically calling out falling house prices and stagnant real wages (wages that aren't keeping up with inflation). This kind of internal dissent is unusual and suggests there's growing unease within Labor about whether the government's economic narrative is landing with voters. It's a political headache for Albanese heading into the next election cycle.

stories.title: Labor ditches new packaging laws to cut plastic waste, sparking unprecedented 'scale and breadth of outrage'
stories.why_it_matters: The Labor government has quietly dropped planned laws that would have required companies to use more recycled content in packaging and reduce plastic waste. The Guardian reports this has triggered an 'unprecedented scale and breadth of outrage' from environmental groups, industry bodies, and state governments alike — an unusually broad coalition of critics. The backflip appears to have been driven by industry lobbying, and it's a political embarrassment for a government that campaigned on environmental action.

ai.summary: AI governance is front and centre this weekend — the CEOs of the world's biggest AI companies are jointly pushing governments to regulate AI development, while inside those same companies, there are serious internal debates about existential risk. Google's Gemini 3.5 Flash has quietly arrived as a competitive model.

stories.title: OpenAI, Anthropic CEOs Propose AI Development 'Brake'
stories.why_it_matters: The heads of OpenAI and Anthropic — two of the most powerful AI companies in the world — are jointly proposing that governments install an 'emergency brake' mechanism on AI development. The idea is that if AI systems start behaving in dangerous or unpredictable ways, there's a legal mechanism to slow or halt progress. This is significant because it's the AI industry's own leaders saying the technology needs guardrails — not just outside critics.

stories.title: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Microsoft CEOs Ask Congress to Mandate Synthetic DNA Screening
stories.why_it_matters: In an unusual joint move, the CEOs of OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Microsoft have all gone to the US Congress to demand mandatory screening of synthetic DNA — artificial genetic material that could be designed using AI to create dangerous pathogens (disease-causing agents). They're worried AI could be used to help bad actors design biological weapons, and they want a legal requirement for labs to screen DNA orders. This is the tech giants voluntarily seeking regulation of their own tools — a rare and notable moment.

stories.title: Inside the Discussions at AI Companies Over a Superintelligence Doomsday
stories.why_it_matters: The New York Times has published a rare inside look at conversations happening within leading AI labs about 'superintelligence' — AI that surpasses human intelligence in every domain. Researchers are debating how likely catastrophic outcomes are and what safeguards exist. The fact that these conversations are happening now — not in some theoretical future — gives context to why the CEOs are pushing governments so hard for regulation.

stories.title: Gemini 3.5 Flash Lands 2 Points Behind Claude Opus 4.7 At A Third Of The Cost
stories.why_it_matters: Google has quietly released Gemini 3.5 Flash, a new AI model that scores almost as well as Anthropic's top-tier Claude Opus 4.7 on benchmark tests — but costs just one-third as much to run. This is significant for businesses using AI: more capable AI at lower cost accelerates adoption. For Google (which you hold via GOOG), this is a sign the company is competing seriously in the AI model race, not just relying on search revenue.

stories.title: US Legislators Push AI Safety Laws Amid Human Extinction Warnings
stories.why_it_matters: US Congress members are now actively drafting AI safety legislation, with some legislators citing warnings from AI researchers about risks to humanity — including the possibility of AI systems causing large-scale harm. Al Jazeera reports the debate is intensifying after tech CEOs raised alarms directly with Congress. For investors in AI-exposed stocks (GOOG, MSFT, GXAI), regulation could create short-term uncertainty but also longer-term market stability.

sport.summary: NRL Finals Week 1 is wrapping up with some big results — the Dolphins and Sharks both winning, and the Panthers vs Roosters blockbuster still live in the second half. In AFL, Taylor Walker played his final game amid an emotional weekend, while the US Open women's final delivered a thriller.

stories.title: Dolphins stun Warriors 26-16 in fiery Finals Week 1 thriller
stories.why_it_matters: The Dolphins made history with a 26-16 win over the Warriors at Go Media Stadium in Auckland on Saturday, ending the Warriors' finals campaign. It's a significant result for the Dolphins, who are still a young club building their finals pedigree. The Warriors, playing at home, were stunned — a heartbreaker for their fans.

stories.title: Sharks beat Cowboys 26-16 — Trindall returns from shoulder dislocation to lead the way
stories.why_it_matters: The Cronulla Sharks knocked out the Cowboys 26-16 at Allianz Stadium on Saturday night. The big story was Nicho Trindall returning from a shoulder dislocation to guide the Sharks — a gutsy comeback performance from their halfback. The Cowboys' season is over. The Sharks advance.

stories.title: Panthers vs Roosters finals blockbuster — live in the 2nd half
stories.why_it_matters: Panthers vs Roosters was locked at 12-12 at half-time in Sunday's Finals Week 1 blockbuster at CommBank Stadium — this one is going right down to the wire. A Panthers star reportedly made a fiery statement after a 'surprise blunder', adding some drama to an already tense finals clash. Result still to come.

stories.title: AFL world rallies around Hawthorn star after 'devastating' scenes; Taylor Walker's final game
stories.why_it_matters: It was an emotional weekend in AFL. Taylor Walker — one of Adelaide's most beloved players — played what appears to be his final career game, with Brisbane's Dayne Zorko receiving widespread praise for a touching gesture toward Walker after the match. Separately, a Hawthorn star suffered what's being described as 'devastating' scenes, drawing an outpouring from the football community. AFL finals are heating up.

stories.title: Elena Rybakina beats Aryna Sabalenka to win 2026 US Open women's title
stories.why_it_matters: Kazakhstan's Elena Rybakina defeated World No.1 Aryna Sabalenka to claim the 2026 US Open women's title in New York on Saturday. It's a massive win for Rybakina, who beat the favourite in what has been one of the year's most anticipated Grand Slam finals. Sabalenka had been dominant all year — this result shakes up the women's tennis rankings heading into the end-of-season stretch.
